title: Procurement Sourcing Strategy for Major Spend Categories: Spend Analysis, Make‑vs‑Buy Assessment, Supplier Selection Criteria and Contracting Approach
subtitle: Category Sourcing Strategy | Spend Analysis · Make‑vs‑Buy · Preferred Supplier Criteria & Contracting Approach

document_brief.narrative_theme: Use FY2025 category spend insights to decide what to make versus buy, narrow to a defensible set of preferred suppliers, and apply a contracting approach that delivers measurable savings and risk reduction for the enterprise’s IT Services spend.

structure.caption: Figure 6: IT Services Sourcing Notes — FY2025 Review

spec.title: IT Services Sourcing Notes — FY2025 Review
lines: Total FY2025 IT Services spend: $142.8M (↑11% vs FY2024)
Top 5 suppliers = 67% of total spend → concentration risk
Ad-hoc SOW engagements ~$18M (fragmented, high rate variance)
Make vs Buy assessment:
- Core app maintenance (Tier 1 systems) → consider insourcing (est. 18% cost reduction)
- Cloud migration + niche cyber skills → continue external (skills gap internally)
- PMO augmentation → reduce external by 40%, build internal bench
Rate benchmarking (external):
hr → target 10–12% rate correction
hr (market ~$180) → negotiate volume discount
Preferred supplier shortlist (target 4 strategic partners):
1) BlueRidge Tech (strong in app dev, good SLA history)
2) Northstar Digital (cloud + DevOps depth)
3) Kestrel Cyber Advisory (specialized security capability)
4) Vertex Solutions (regional coverage, competitive rates)
Selection criteria weighting:
- Cost competitiveness 30%
- Technical capability 25%
compliance maturity 20%
- Delivery performance 15%
- Innovation roadmap 10%
Contracting approach:
rate cards + KPI-linked rebates (3–5%)
annual rate review + benchmarking clause
- Volume tiers for blended rate reductions
- Stronger SLA credits (uptime, defect density, response time)
Savings target: $14–18M over 3 yrs (~9–12% of addressable spend)
Risk reduction: fewer suppliers (22 → 8), standardized security terms
